alternatives.argument: Define shortest accepting-branch time for the finite-branching machine interface, with infinity when no branch accepts. Interleave the acceptor with a deterministic exact clock on disjoint tapes; accept before expiry and reject at expiry. This preserves the cutoff language and gives an all-branch O(n+T(n)) bound while keeping shortest acceptance distinct from maximum branch time.

Guess the chronological displays and actions of an accepting branch, then make one verification pass per virtual tape, checking each cell history, head visit, write, state transition, and clamped-left move. A genuine t-step branch yields O_M(n+t) symbols and passes; local consistency reconstructs a genuine branch. The fixed number of passes gives linear acceptance time.

Extend the published self-delimiting finite-table code by encoding finite transition-option lists and a unique terminal delimiter. The interpreter rejects malformed prefixes, chooses only encoded transitions, and updates two simulated tapes. For fixed code e, parsing and every simulation macro have fixed cost, giving c_e(|x|+tau_M(x))+d_e; nonacceptance creates no accepting interpreter branch.

Translate the nondeterministic syntax to a deterministic dovetailing recognizer, apply the published s-m-n and Kleene fixed-point theorems to the total compiler, and translate the fixed finite index back to a literal prefix. The recursion theorem supplies language equality only; fixed quantitative overhead follows separately from the concrete hard-wiring compiler and prefix interpreter.

For union choose a component; for intersection copy the input and guess accepting branches sequentially; for cutoff interleave the acceptor with an exact clock and suppress late acceptance. Normalize tape count with the two-tape verifier. Direct branch analysis proves both language directions and the stated minimum, sum, and fixed-factor bounds, including short inputs.

Enumerate pairs of a coded finite-branching machine and a positive constant, assign each a distinct unary length, exhaust its finite computation tree through c b(n) steps, and choose the opposite membership answer. The language is recursive because b is total recursive and each bounded tree is finite. Any O(b) acceptor, after enlarging its constant over finitely many short inputs, contradicts its assigned length.

Use the quantitative fixed point to build one acceptor whose recursively padded cutoffs confront the next coded competitor. Define both padding sequences by least recursive searches using the exact clock and a(n+1)=o(T(n)), after fixing every simulator, copy, and clock constant. Induction keeps each cutoff within a fixed fraction of the next T budget and transfers any O(a) acceptance claim to one recursive bound covering every recursive unary language, contradicting the unary diagonal lemma. Clock the final machine and handle the finite initial segment explicitly.

Take an explicit k-level nested-loop exact clock T_k=Theta((n+1)^k) and a(n)=max(n,ceil((n+1)^k/log_2(n+2))). Then a is total recursive, a>=n, and a(n+1)=o(T_k(n)); recursive-padding separation gives nonmembership, and constant-factor invariance gives the displayed proper containment.

Use a two-choice machine with a one-step accepting branch and a branch moving right forever. Its shortest acceptance time is one although worst-branch time is undefined. Product it with a small exact clock; enumerating product branches proves preservation of the cutoff language and all-branch halting with fixed scheduling overhead.
